content: The French inhale is a smoking technique that involves taking a deep inhalation of smoke into the mouth. With the mouth open, the smoke is allowed to drift out passively. Simultaneously, the individual inhales through the nose, drawing the smoke upward from the mouth into the nasal passages. This creates the visual effect of smoke appearing to flow upward, which some colloquially refer to as an Irish Waterfall, a term rooted in the stereotype that Irish phenomena are reversed or unconventional. This technique is frequently combined with the creation of smoke rings to enhance the visual display.
